relations.name: Round-trip fidelity
preconditions: selected carrier and key are supported
relations.source_case: Build one marked artifact for payload p under key k.
relations.follow_up: Extract from that artifact under k.
relations.oracle: The extracted bytes equal p exactly.

relations.name: Host-semantic preservation
preconditions: embedding is declared semantics-preserving for the selected observations
relations.follow_up: Independently build and execute the marked host on the frozen inputs.
relations.oracle: Every normalized marked output equals its unmarked counterpart.

relations.name: Unmarked rejection
preconditions: absence is not an accepted public default
relations.follow_up: Attempt extraction with a syntactically valid key.
relations.oracle: Extraction returns a normalized rejection outcome.

relations.name: Wrong-key rejection
relations.source_case: Construct and independently validate a carrier for p under k1.
relations.follow_up: Invoke the subject extractor on the same artifact under k2.

upstream_guard.interpretation: The upstream operator is disabled to isolate the negative antecedent. These rows are admitted antecedent checks, not fault-active executions.

relations.name: Payload separation
relations.source_case: Build artifact a1 for p1 under k.
relations.follow_up: Build a2 for p2 under k and extract both artifacts.
relations.oracle: a1 yields p1, a2 yields p2, and the extracted values differ.

relations.name: Cross-compiler invariance
preconditions: GCC and Clang are supported for the selected host and carrier
relations.follow_up: Build the same request with Clang at O2.
relations.oracle: Both extract p and their host observations agree.
relations.admission: Both requested compiler configurations must be supported and actually realized.

relations.name: Optimization invariance
preconditions: O0, O2, and Os are supported
relations.oracle: All three extract p and agree on host observations.

relations.name: Clean-room relocation
preconditions: the binary is declared self-contained and path-independent
relations.source_case: Build and validate one marked artifact.
relations.follow_up: Copy and rename only the binary into a clean directory.
relations.oracle: The relocated binary still extracts p.

relations.name: Carrier-removal rejection
preconditions: the selected transform removes the only accepted carrier
relations.source_case: Construct a valid antecedent carrier under an upstream guard.
relations.follow_up: Apply carrier-specific removal and invoke the subject extractor.

upstream_guard.interpretation: The upstream operator is disabled to isolate the negative antecedent. These rows are admitted antecedent checks, not fault-active executions.

relations.name: Carrier-corruption rejection
preconditions: integrity validation is part of extraction
relations.source_case: Construct a valid antecedent carrier under an upstream guard.
relations.follow_up: Change checksum material without changing the intended payload.

upstream_guard.interpretation: The upstream operator is disabled to isolate the negative antecedent. These rows are admitted antecedent checks, not fault-active executions.

relations.name: Requested/actual trace agreement
preconditions: the build emits auditable requested and actual settings
relations.oracle: Actual compiler and optimization equal the request.
relations.direct_verdict: Requested and realized compiler/optimization fields must agree; this relation directly judges configuration fidelity.

relations.name: Interleaved artifact isolation
preconditions: two builds may share one process without semantic aliasing
relations.source_case: Submit two distinct payload requests p1 and p2 concurrently to one pipeline instance.
relations.follow_up: Rendezvous both requests at staging before either compilation proceeds. Complete both overlapping builds a1 and a2, then extract both artifacts.
relations.oracle: Each artifact yields its own payload.

relations.name: Extraction-revisit independence
preconditions: extraction depends only on declared immutable context
relations.source_case: Build a1 for p1 and a2 for p2, then extract a1; both builds use key-alpha, GCC and O2.
relations.follow_up: Extract a2, then revisit a1: B1 B2 X1 X2 X1.
relations.oracle: The three extractions equal p1, p2, p1 respectively.
relations.handler_scope: handler names the historical Boolean adapter; sequence_contract describes the evidence-gated handler
relations.sequence_contract: The evidence-gated handler executes B1 B2 X1 X2 X1, changing only payload while holding key, compiler and optimization fixed. It is not reverse-order extraction. The historical Boolean handler executes B1 X1 B2 X2 X1 and changes the second key; its protocol is not substituted for the current handler.

relations.name: Rebuild stability
preconditions: the two build requests are identical
relations.follow_up: Repeat r to build a2 and extract both.
relations.oracle: Both artifacts yield p; byte identity is not required.
